lines.text: EXACTA SVMMA HIC,
euidensqúe Musicæ.
VNiuersum hoc, antiqui Musica
contineri perhibuerunt. Nihil e-
nim in rerum natura absque com-
mensuratione et proportione con-
sistit: neque quicquam eorum quæ
fiunt, sine debita commensuratione et propor-
tione si fiat, rectè productum natumúe esse di-
citur: siue id ab arte efficiatur, siue à natura: et
siue sub sensum illud cadat, siue solo intellectu
perspiciatur.
Cæterùm Musica ipsa per se commensura-
tio quædam omnino et proportionalitas est, ni-
mirum harmonia uniuersi existens. Fortassis et
ipsam diuinam naturam haud inconuenienter sui
ipsius et uniuersi harmoniam quispiam dixerit:
siquidem in Deo concinnatus, et ad consonan-
tiam coaptatus mundus, bene, atque adeò quàm
optimè se habere uidetur. Tanto nimirum Mu-
sicam illi dignati sunt miraculo. Ea quando in
omnibus conspicitur, atque uniuersa temperat, e-
xornatqúe, tum sensui uoluptatem, congruentiam
autem (harmoniam dico) Naturæ, beatitatem
denique intellectui largitur: nos de ea Musica quæ
in sensibus, aut potius uno sensuum auditu con-
sideratur, paucis disseremus.
Sonus est, uocis nullo interuallo diuisæ har-
moniæ particeps intensio, seu tenor. Interuallum
autem, sonorum mutua unius ad alterum ratio,
siue respectus. Systema, complexus est certus
interuallorum. Harmonia, ipsa constructio sy-
stematum. Enimuerò sonus diuisionis capax
non est, ut neque punctum in Geometria. Har-
moniæ participem diximus, quia ita effertur, ut
possit etiam cum alio sono ad harmoniam con-
cinnari. Quod nisi fiat, iam is dissonus sit sonus,
non consonus: imò neque sonus dicetur esse, sed stre
pitus quispiam temerè editus, et ad consonan-
tiam nulli existens usui. Proinde diuersæ sunt
sonorum, quas illi progressu et ordine, quem à
graui ad acutum obseruant, nanciscuntur no-
menclationes: Proslambanomenos, Hypate hy-
paton, parhypate hypaton, hypate diatonos, hy-
pate meson, parhypate meson, diatonos meson,
mese monos, paramesos, trite diezeugmene, dia-
tonos diezeugmene, nete diezeugmene, trite
hyperbolæon, diatonos hyperbolæon, nete hy-
perbolæon. Per has sonorum species heccæde
cachordum, hoc est, sedecim chordarum instru-
mentum in quindecim fidibus instructo organo
(Pentecædecachordum uocant Græci) absol-
uitur, fine octachordi ad principium sequentium
continuò assumpto. Quam enim rationem ha-
bet primus sonus ad octauum, eandem octauus
ad decimumquintum obtinet. Et hæc de sonis.
Interuallorum autem minimum genus est,
quod diesin uocant: deinde semitonium, cuius du-
pla ad acutum est accessio, respectu dieseos. De-
inde est tonus duplici constans semitonio, et ra-
tionem sesquioctauam constituens, ut est noue-
narij ad octonarium numerum. Quo fit, ut semi
tonium sit quasi dimidium sesquioctauæ diesis au-
tem quasi quadrans eiusdem. Quamuis enim ra
tione numeri unitas diuidi non potest, utique tamen
unitas quæ in materia conspicitur, diuiditur Geo-
metricè. Nam chordam eam quæ obseruat ra-
tionem sesquioctauam, possibile est diuidi in semi
sesquioctauam, quod est semitonium, et hoc de-
nuò diuidi in diesin. Geometriæ enim est, semper
à maiori recta minorem posse detrahere, sem-
perqúe posse minori apponere maiorem. ex quo se-
quitur, ut quælibet figura ad placitum possit cùm
augeri, tum diminui. Id uerò in Arithmetica lo-
cum non habet. Ad hæc, propositum quadratum
in æqualia partiri quadrata, aut duplum efficere
non potest. Numerorum enim sedecim, qui est
quadratus, neque in duo potest diducere quadra
ta (octo enim Arithmeticè quadratum esse, aut
eius numeri dare radicem quadratam, impos-
sibile est) neque duplum eius aliud quadratum
dare (fieri enim non potest, ut numerus triginta
duo sit quadratus) At Geometriæ hoc factu
non est difficile. nam Geometer dati quadrati la
tere loco diametri accepto, ubi circumposuit qua-
dratum, id statim propositi est dimidium: iterumqúe acce
pta dati quadrati diametro loco lateris, ex eo qua
dratum describet, quod propositum dupli esse constat.
Sic etiam sesquioctaua toni proportio diuidi poterit
in semitonium, iterúmque in diesin. Eorundem
quoque auctione, compositæ quoque reliquæ in-
teruallorum species constituuntur: tridiesis, tri-
semitonium, ditonus, tritonus, et quo quis mo-
do uoluerit, idqúe rhythmus admiserit, ueluti ex
sequentibus cognoscetur. Incomposita autem
dicuntur, quia tanquam una cantilena ex coale-
scentibus in unum tribus diesibus, aut semito-
nijs totidem, aut diuersis tonis conflatur, po-
tentia quidem siue facultate diuersa interualla
continens, sed unico tamen interuallo edita.
Præter hæc sunt et alia interualla: diatessaron,
quartam uulgò dicunt: diapente, ijsdem quinta est:
et diapason, quam trito uocabulo octauam no-
minant. Hæc autem neque immediata sunt, neque
incomposita, sed per media omnia dicta interual-
la transeunt. Atque hæc quidem interualla dicun-
tur, ratione sonitus qui est à primo sono ad extre
mum: quantitate autem intermediorum sonorum
huiusmodi appellationes inuenerunt, diatessaron
quidem, quia per quatuor sonos aut neruos tran-
sit: diapente, quia per quinque: diapason, quia per
omnes, hoc est, per octo. Nam quia omnia inter-
ualla complentur in octachordo, atque inde i-
terum geminantur, diapason dicitur, quod per o-
cto neruos transit. Argumento sunt etiam no-
mina, quæ sequentibus interuallis obtigerunt, ut

pente: disdiapason, hoc est, octaua cum quarta, o-

running_text:
EXACTA SVMMA HIC, euidensqúe Musicæ.

Vniuersum hoc, antiqui Musica contineri perhibuerunt. Nihil enim in rerum natura absque commensuratione et proportione consistit: neque quicquam eorum quæ fiunt, sine debita commensuratione et proportione si fiat, rectè productum natumúe esse dicitur: siue id ab arte efficiatur, siue à natura: et siue sub sensum illud cadat, siue solo intellectu perspiciatur.

Cæterùm Musica ipsa per se commensuratio quædam omnino et proportionalitas est, nimirum harmonia uniuersi existens. Fortassis et ipsam diuinam naturam haud inconuenienter sui ipsius et uniuersi harmoniam quispiam dixerit: siquidem in Deo concinnatus, et ad consonantiam coaptatus mundus, bene, atque adeò quàm optimè se habere uidetur. Tanto nimirum Musicam illi dignati sunt miraculo. Ea quando in omnibus conspicitur, atque uniuersa temperat, exornatqúe, tum sensui uoluptatem, congruentiam autem (harmoniam dico) Naturæ, beatitatem denique intellectui largitur: nos de ea Musica quæ in sensibus, aut potius uno sensuum auditu consideratur, paucis disseremus.

Sonus est, uocis nullo interuallo diuisæ harmoniæ particeps intensio, seu tenor. Interuallum autem, sonorum mutua unius ad alterum ratio, siue respectus. Systema, complexus est certus interuallorum. Harmonia, ipsa constructio systematum. Enimuerò sonus diuisionis capax non est, ut neque punctum in Geometria. Harmoniæ participem diximus, quia ita effertur, ut possit etiam cum alio sono ad harmoniam concinnari. Quod nisi fiat, iam is dissonus sit sonus, non consonus: imò neque sonus dicetur esse, sed strepitus quispiam temerè editus, et ad consonantiam nulli existens usui. Proinde diuersæ sunt sonorum, quas illi progressu et ordine, quem à graui ad acutum obseruant, nanciscuntur nomenclationes: Proslambanomenos, Hypate hypaton, parhypate hypaton, hypate diatonos, hypate meson, parhypate meson, diatonos meson, mese monos, paramesos, trite diezeugmene, diatonos diezeugmene, nete diezeugmene, trite hyperbolæon, diatonos hyperbolæon, nete hyperbolæon. Per has sonorum species heccædecachordum, hoc est, sedecim chordarum instrumentum in quindecim fidibus instructo organo (Pentecædecachordum uocant Græci) absoluitur, fine octachordi ad principium sequentium continuò assumpto. Quam enim rationem habet primus sonus ad octauum, eandem octauus ad decimumquintum obtinet. Et hæc de sonis.

Interuallorum autem minimum genus est, quod diesin uocant: deinde semitonium, cuius dupla ad acutum est accessio, respectu dieseos. Deinde est tonus duplici constans semitonio, et rationem sesquioctauam constituens, ut est nouenarij ad octonarium numerum. Quo fit, ut semitonium sit quasi dimidium sesquioctauæ diesis autem quasi quadrans eiusdem. Quamuis enim ratione numeri unitas diuidi non potest, utique tamen unitas quæ in materia conspicitur, diuiditur Geometricè. Nam chordam eam quæ obseruat rationem sesquioctauam, possibile est diuidi in semisesquioctauam, quod est semitonium, et hoc denuò diuidi in diesin. Geometriæ enim est, semper à maiori recta minorem posse detrahere, semperqúe posse minori apponere maiorem. ex quo sequitur, ut quælibet figura ad placitum possit cùm augeri, tum diminui. Id uerò in Arithmetica locum non habet. Ad hæc, propositum quadratum in æqualia partiri quadrata, aut duplum efficere non potest. Numerorum enim sedecim, qui est quadratus, neque in duo potest diducere quadrata (octo enim Arithmeticè quadratum esse, aut eius numeri dare radicem quadratam, impossibile est) neque duplum eius aliud quadratum dare (fieri enim non potest, ut numerus triginta duo sit quadratus) At Geometriæ hoc factu non est difficile. nam Geometer dati quadrati latere loco diametri accepto, ubi circumposuit quadratum, id statim propositi est dimidium: iterumqúe accepta dati quadrati diametro loco lateris, ex eo quadratum describet, quod propositum dupli esse constat. Sic etiam sesquioctaua toni proportio diuidi poterit in semitonium, iterúmque in diesin. Eorundem quoque auctione, compositæ quoque reliquæ interuallorum species constituuntur: tridiesis, trisemitonium, ditonus, tritonus, et quo quis modo uoluerit, idqúe rhythmus admiserit, ueluti ex sequentibus cognoscetur. Incomposita autem dicuntur, quia tanquam una cantilena ex coalescentibus in unum tribus diesibus, aut semitonijs totidem, aut diuersis tonis conflatur, potentia quidem siue facultate diuersa interualla continens, sed unico tamen interuallo edita. Præter hæc sunt et alia interualla: diatessaron, quartam uulgò dicunt: diapente, ijsdem quinta est: et diapason, quam trito uocabulo octauam nominant. Hæc autem neque immediata sunt, neque incomposita, sed per media omnia dicta interualla transeunt. Atque hæc quidem interualla dicuntur, ratione sonitus qui est à primo sono ad extremum: quantitate autem intermediorum sonorum huiusmodi appellationes inuenerunt, diatessaron quidem, quia per quatuor sonos aut neruos transit: diapente, quia per quinque: diapason, quia per omnes, hoc est, per octo. Nam quia omnia interualla complentur in octachordo, atque inde iterum geminantur, diapason dicitur, quod per octo neruos transit. Argumento sunt etiam nomina, quæ sequentibus interuallis obtigerunt, ut sunt diapason cum diatessaron, diapason cum diapente: disdiapason, hoc est, octaua cum quarta, octaua cum quinta, et duæ octauæ.

notes.comment: Section title in two lines: spaced roman capitals, then larger roman lower case. The enclitic is the abbreviation q́; (q with acute + semicolon sign), expanded qúe (see conventions).
Large decorated woodcut initial V (foliage and a figure), five lines high: lines 3-7 are set beside it; the text continues with capital N.
Macron over e = n; tilde over o = n.
Abbreviation with full stop.
e-/xornatqúe hyphenated across lines 22-23.
Catchword at bottom right, repeated as the first word of p. 41.
No hyphen printed at line end (line runs to the margin).

Clearly printed 'hypate diatonos'. Not a slip of the Latin: the Greek of this edition (p. 25, line 6) reads likewise 'ὑπάτη διάτονος' between 'παρυπάτη ὑπάτων' and 'ὑπάτη μέσων'; Xylander transliterates the Greek as printed.

Printed clearly. Greek p. 25, lines 7-8: '* μέση μόνως, παραμέσος' (sic), with Xylander's marginal note '* διάτονος μέσων addo'. So 'mese monos, paramesos' renders the printed Greek, and 'diatonos meson' in line 21 is Xylander's own supplement, flagged in the Greek margin.
No hyphen at the end of p. 41, though the catchword is 'cachor-'.
Signature 'c 5' at bottom centre; catchword 'cachor-' at bottom right.
No punctuation printed between 'sesquioctauæ' and 'diesis' (a comma would be expected); transcribed as printed.

notes.what: word broken without hyphen (join supported by the Greek)
notes.comment: No hyphen; joined in the running text as one word 'semisesquioctauam' ('half-sesquioctave', glossed 'quod est semitonium'); could also be two words 'semi sesquioctauam'. The Greek (p. 26, line 5) has the single compound 'εἰς ἡμιεπόγδοον', which supports the one-word join 'semisesquioctauam'.
q́; with acute expanded qúe.
Catchword at bottom right, repeated at the top of p. 43.

notes.printed: Numerorum enim ſedecim, qui eſt quadratus
notes.comment: Clearly printed 'Numerorum' (verified at 3x). The Greek (p. 26, line 16) has the accusative singular 'τὸν γὰρ ἑξκαιδέκατον ἀριθμὸν τετράγωνον ὄντα', so 'Numerum' is the expected Latin; probably a misprint, transcribed as printed.
The i is broken (looks like a colon); 'diducere' is the natural reading.

notes.printed: two dot figures in the outer (right) margin beside lines 4-14
notes.reading: Figure 1 (beside lines 4-7): 16 dots in a 4 x 4 square, with a horizontal rule across the middle dividing it into two rectangles of 2 x 4 = 8 dots. Figure 2 (beside lines 8-14): 32 dots = two 4 x 4 squares one above the other, separated by a horizontal rule.
notes.comment: Illustrates the text: 16 is square but cannot be divided into two square numbers (8 is not square), and its double 32 is not square. No numerals or words in the figures.
A 5 x 3 px blot above the o of 'Geometer' is far smaller than the accents of this fount; taken as a speck, not an accent.

notes.printed: dratū,id ſtatim propoſiti eſt dimidiū:iterūq́; acce
notes.reading: dratum, id statim propositi est dimidium: iterumqúe acce
notes.comment: 'acce | pta' broken without hyphen (joined 'accepta').

notes.printed: dratū deſcribet,quod propoſitū dupli eſſe cōſtat.
notes.reading: dratum describet, quod propositum dupli esse constat.

notes.comment: Line not indented, so not marked as a new paragraph. 'diuidipoterit' is set tight; read as two words.
Catchword at bottom right; p. 44 begins 'continens'. Mirror-image show-through of the marginal note 'Vide Annotationes' from p. 44 appears in the right margin and is ignored.
Line 1 ends about one em short of the measure and 'Præter hæc' begins a new topic, but line 2 is not indented, so it is not marked as a paragraph start.
'ijsdem' (= iisdem) kept as printed.

Roman type in the left (outer) margin beside lines 17-18; refers to Xylander's annotations. The dots in the left margin of this scan are show-through of the p. 43 figures. No hyphen is printed after 'Anno' (verified at 4x).
'diateßaron' in this line: ß = ss.

The mark has a head set slightly above the baseline and a short straight tail (about 7 px). It is not the curved comma of 'quinta,' in the same line (tail about 11 px, curving left), but it has the same shape as the line-final stop after 'edita.' on p. 44 line 1, which certainly ends a sentence. Read as full stop; the paragraph ends here (next line indented).
'cōſonan' expanded consonan; 'Paraphonū' (l. 23) expanded Paraphonum.
Word continues on p. 45 (next chunk): 'secundum'. Catchword 'dum' at bottom right not transcribed as a line.

conventions: Long s -> s; ß (long s + s) -> ss; ct / st / ss ligatures resolved; æ and œ kept as printed.
u/v and i/j kept as printed (uniuersi, nouenarij, semitonijs, ijsdem); capitals as printed (SVMMA).
Ampersand & expanded to 'et' throughout (17 occurrences in this chunk).

q; (q + semicolon sign) expanded 'que' (absque, neque, atque, utique, quoque, denique). q́; (q with an acute, the printers' mark of the enclitic -que) expanded 'qúe' (euidensqúe, exornatqúe, semperqúe, iterumqúe), matching the fully printed forms 'idqúe', 'natumúe'.
Macron/tilde over a vowel expanded to m or n (cō- con-, nō non, dimidiū dimidium, etiā etiam, dicūt dicunt, etc.); 'omnib.' -> omnibus.
Accents kept as printed (rectè, à, quàm, adeò, optimè, Cæterùm, imò, temerè, Enimuerò, continuò, denuò, cùm, uerò, uulgò, Arithmeticè, metricè, iterúmque, natumúe, idqúe).

Spacing around punctuation normalised (no space before, one after; '( harmoniam dico )' -> '(harmoniam dico)'); wider spaces the printer leaves between some sentences are not marked and not treated as paragraph breaks.

Running heads, page numbers, signatures and catchwords are not counted as text lines; lines_printed counts the lines transcribed for the page, including the two heading lines on p. 40 (22 body lines + 2 heading lines).
Words broken at line end WITHOUT a printed hyphen (the compositor ran to the margin) are transcribed without '-' and listed in notes; they are joined in running_text.
In running_text the decorated initial is written 'Vniuersum' (lines: 'VNiuersum') and the two heading lines are joined on one line.

changes.reason: The marginal note has no hyphen after 'Anno'; the line break is unmarked in print.
Measured on the scan: the four dot rows of figure 1 stand level with lines 4, 5, 6 and between 6/7 (rule between lines 5 and 6); figure 2 (lines 8-14) is correct.
Checked against Greek p. 25 (gr-seq191-p25.jpg): the Greek also has ὑπάτη διάτονος, so the Latin reading is not a misprint.
Checked against Greek p. 25: μέση μόνως, παραμέσος; the marginal note '* διάτονος μέσων addo' explains 'diatonos meson' (l. 21).

changes.before: notes.what: word broken without hyphen (debatable join)
changes.after: notes.what: word broken without hyphen (join supported by the Greek)
changes.reason: Greek p. 26 reads ἡμιεπόγδοον (one word), supporting the join in running_text.

changes.after: notes.comment: Greek τὸν ... ἀριθμόν (acc. sg.) cited; reading kept 'Numerorum' as printed.
changes.reason: Greek checked: it supports 'Numerum', but the Latin print is unambiguous, so the transcription stays as printed.

changes.before: notes.comment: looks like a comma ... read as full stop
changes.after: notes.comment: same glyph shape as the certain stop 'edita.' (p. 44 l. 1); full stop confirmed
changes.reason: Pixel comparison with the comma in 'quinta,' (same line) and the stops after 'perspiciatur.' (p. 40) and 'edita.' (p. 44).

changes.after: notes: speck above o of 'Geometer' recorded, not transcribed
changes.reason: Records the mark so that a later reader does not take it for a missed accent.

still_uncertain: p. 44 l. 20 'octauæ.': the mark is ambiguous between a stop and a comma; the glyph shape matches the stop after 'edita.' (p. 44 l. 1), so the reading is a full stop. A comma remains possible.
p. 43 l. 3 'Numerorum': clearly printed. The Greek (acc. sg. ἀριθμόν) suggests that 'Numerum' was meant; a probable misprint, kept as printed.

Word division where the print sets words tight (p. 43 l. 15 'diuidipoterit', p. 43 l. 13 'locolateris', p. 42 l. 21 'diuidiin', p. 40 l. 13 'ipsaper'): these are separated as the words require, which is an editorial decision, not a reading.
verification.notes: I checked all 124 lines of pp. 40-44 word by word against crops enlarged 1.7-7x: every abbreviation (q; / q́; / macron / omnib.), accent (all graves and the acutes on -úe/-qúe), ß/long-s resolution, line-end hyphen, paragraph indent, heading, catchword and signature. No error was found in any line text, line break, paragraph start or in running_text. I rebuilt running_text from the lines with a script and it matches exactly, and the 17 '&' → 'et' expansions match the prints. All changes are to the notes: one wrong 'printed' form (a hyphen added to the marginal note on p. 44), a small correction to the position of the figure on p. 43, and four uncertain notes resolved or supported by the Greek of the same edition (pp. 25-26).
